variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning (RAFT) is a supervised fine-tuning recipe for a language model that will answer questions with documents retrieved from a known domain. Each training record pairs a question with answer-bearing oracle documents, irrelevant or misleading distractor documents, and a target answer grounded in the oracle.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Four terms define the recipe”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Oracle document
pairs.detail: A passage from which the target answer can be supported.
pairs.explanation: A passage from which the target answer can be supported. One question may require more than one oracle.

pairs.label: Distractor document
pairs.detail: A passage that does not support the answer.
pairs.explanation: A passage that does not support the answer. Hard distractors are plausible enough to test real evidence selection.

pairs.label: P fraction
pairs.detail: The share of training questions whose retrieved context retains an oracle.
pairs.explanation: The share of training questions whose retrieved context retains an oracle. The remaining share contains only distractors.

pairs.label: Evidence target
pairs.detail: The answer demonstrates which text supports the claim, often with a concise rationale and an extractive quotation.
pairs.explanation: The answer demonstrates which text supports the claim, often with a concise rationale and an extractive quotation.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is: train and evaluate on the retrieval conditions the deployed generator must actually handle.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Oracle document: A passage from which the target answer can be supported. Distractor document: A passage that does not support the answer. P fraction: The share of training questions whose retrieved context retains an oracle. Evidence target: The answer demonstrates which text supports the claim, often with a concise rationale and an extractive quotation.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Build records from the production retrieval path”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Freeze the retrieval profile
pairs.detail: Record the corpus snapshot, chunker, metadata filters, embedding model, reranker, and top-k used to retrieve passages.
pairs.explanation: Record the corpus snapshot, chunker, metadata filters, embedding model, reranker, and top-k used to retrieve passages.

pairs.label: Create answerable questions
pairs.detail: Cover real user intents and difficult domain distinctions.
pairs.explanation: Cover real user intents and difficult domain distinctions. Split by source or topic so near-duplicates do not leak across evaluation.

pairs.label: Label oracle evidence
pairs.detail: Identify every passage required to support the answer and verify the target against the source.
pairs.explanation: Identify every passage required to support the answer and verify the target against the source.

pairs.label: Sample realistic distractors
pairs.detail: Use confusing passages returned by the retriever, not only random text that the model can dismiss trivially.
pairs.explanation: Use confusing passages returned by the retriever, not only random text that the model can dismiss trivially.

pairs.detail: Store question, passage IDs, oracle presence, target, retrieval profile, generator, prompt, and quality-review identity.
pairs.explanation: Store question, passage IDs, oracle presence, target, retrieval profile, generator, prompt, and quality-review identity.

variants.prompt: What does RAFT change in a domain-specific RAG system?
options: It fine-tunes the generator to use answer-bearing documents and resist distractors in an open-book setting.
It removes the retriever and stores every document in model weights.
It guarantees that the top-ranked passage contains the answer.
It trains only the embedding model used for retrieval.
variants.explanation: RAFT adapts the generator for retrieved in-domain context. Retrieval remains a separate production dependency.

variants.prompt: Why should hard distractors come from the production retrieval distribution?

They always reduce the token count of each example.

They make retriever recall unimportant.

variants.prompt: Does an oracle-absent RAFT example automatically teach the model to abstain?
options: No. Canonical RAFT still targets the answer, so abstention requires explicit labels and separate evaluation.
Yes. Any missing oracle forces an abstention target.
Yes, but only when top-k is greater than five.
No, because RAFT cannot represent missing evidence.
variants.explanation: Oracle absence and abstention are different behaviors. The original recipe applies memorization pressure by keeping the answer target.
